title: P-006 / AUTO-BAR-R-03-P-006 — targeted L4 mutation proof (plan-class-risk-floor)

whyL4IsRequired.mechanism: spec-test-adequacy.ts requiredProofFloor() returns 'l4' when HIGH_RISK_BEHAVIOR_CLASSES includes the clause's behaviorClass; 'lifecycle' is a member. AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-006 is behaviorClass 'happy-path' and carries no such floor.
whyL4IsRequired.note: This row exists because a PASSING journey does not by itself show the journey can FAIL. The mutation below establishes red capability.

mutation.targets: The exact identity the R-03 journey asserts: 'restores the SAME native conversation after the operator OS process exits'. The mutant binds the restored session to a fresh id, so resume restores a DIFFERENT conversation.
preconditionsVerifiedBeforeLaunch: target string occurs EXACTLY once in the file (a multi-site mutation would not be targeted)
mutation sits AFTER the identity guard at lines 39-48, so the guard does not short-circuit it
randomUUID is already imported at line 4, so the mutant still compiles and stays type-correct
su-session-resume.ts is backend-agnostic, so the OMP journey reaches it

probe.tier: in-tree with sweep-lock held (the test reaches the module through the import graph, so copy-out cannot work)

sweepLock.reason: exclude the mutated file from the git-sync sweep for the probe's duration

probe.guardCommand: PUI_REAL_BACKEND=omp PUI_REAL_ACCOUNT=auto npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts -t 'restores the same native conversation after the operator OS process exits'

result.baselineOutcome: PASS — journey green on unmutated source (105252ms)
result.mutantOutcome: FAIL — journey red on mutated source (188000ms)
result.raw: MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=caught expected=caught target=in-tree:lock-held baseline_exit=0 guard_exit=1 mutant_parse=unchecked
result.meaning: The R-03 journey is FALSIFIABLE: it passes on correct source and fails on a targeted break of the exact property it claims to assert. Exit 0 from the probe means the MUTANT WAS CAUGHT, i.e. the guard failed on the mutant — 'probe succeeded' and 'test passed' mean opposite things here.

restoreProof.method: sha256 of the tracked file compared against the fingerprint bound in the P-006 parity artifact — strictly stronger than an empty `git diff`, which on this swept tree only proves the sweep ran

bindableTestRun.testFileResult: TEST_FILE_RESULT requested=1 executed=1 matched=1 status=passed provenance=stamped skippedTests=15
bindableTestRun.whySeparateRun: admin-test-runs-reporter EXCLUDES source='mutation-probe' rows from test_runs (EI-22955349101740344), so the probe's own baseline is NOT bindable. A separate clean unmutated run was executed afterwards to produce a bindable, tenant-stamped row.
bindableTestRun.exclusionCorroboratedEmpirically: Three runs executed in the window 09:23-09:33Z (probe baseline, probe mutant, clean run) but exactly ONE test_runs row exists (17771169), confirming the exclusion rather than assuming it.

fingerprints.algorithm: sha256-file-set-v1 — sha256 over JSON.stringify of the deduped, lexically sorted [{path, sha256}] entry list (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-evidence-store.ts fingerprintRepoFileSet)
fingerprints.positiveControl: The algorithm was validated by RECOMPUTING the previously recorded sourceFingerprint (0b82624b…) from the recorded per-file shas before computing the new value, and independently by reproducing the recorded testFingerprint (f2487e4a…) from the current tree. Both reproduced exactly.

supersedes.reason: The P-006 parity artifact's bound sourceFingerprint (0b82624b…) went stale: exactly 1 of its 7 source files drifted — su-session-claude-engine.ts (bound df4a4f3b…, current 47669f7f…) — because the engine fix landed after binding. The other 6 files are byte-identical.
supersedes.repairable: Yes. Bindings are append-only, so a NEW binding carrying the recomputed fingerprint supersedes the stale rows rather than requiring a new spec revision.
